messages.author: bdbdd16043b71751
messages.subject: Occasion specific trap covariates
parts:
Hello everyone,

I've been banging my head trying to figure out how to get my occasion-specific trap covariates to work in secr.fit.

I'm using a multisession model over three years (2014-2016). The trap data look like this:
# DetectorXYUsageCovariates
A01D306908.39414215521.966111111 /abcdabcdabcd
A02C304412.09354214941.584111111 /cdabcdabcdab
A03B301201.95884210626.937111111 /abcdabcdabcd
...There are 94 traps

The "ab" and "cd" are different bait types that were used at the trap on each of six occasions. 

when I type: "covariates(traps(dataset))", I can see all the trap covariates, but I don't understand how to get them to be treated as occasion-specific covariates.

I've tried "timevaryingcov(covariates(traps(dataset)))"
but I get
> timevaryingcov(covariates(traps(dataset)))
$`2014`
NULL

$`2015`
NULL

$`2016`
NULL

Do you have any advice for how I can get these bait types into the model? I'd like to be able to models such as the following

fit<-secr.fit(dataset, model=list(D~1, g0~bait, sigma~1), CL=F, trapcov=bait, buffer = 20000, trace = FALSE)

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Occasion specific trap covariates
parts:
Kyle

The idea is to associate a set of trap covariates with occasions, and to give the set a name that can be used in a model formula. The specification is saved by 'timevaryingcov' as an attribute of the traps object. In your case I hope this will work:
timevaryingcov(traps(dataset)) <- list(bait = 1:6)
fit  <-secr.fit(dataset, model=list(D~1, g0~bait, sigma~1), buffer = 20000, trace = FALSE)
(associates the first 6 trap covariates with the name 'bait').

It is possible you will run into trouble with multiple sessions, but I hope it works as shown. Unfortunately, using any trap covariates down the fitting (I've lacked motivation to work on speeding it up).
Murray

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Occasion specific trap covariates
parts:
As I feared, the code I gave doesn't work cleanly for multisession capthist. You need to assign the timevaryingcov attribute for each session, something like
for (i in 1:3) timevaryingcov(traps(dataset[[i]])) <- list(bait=1:6)
(for 3 sessions of 6 occasions each).
The trapcov argument is not needed (secr.fit should understand that 'bait' refers to trap covariates).
Murray
